# Research map

## formats

- [`formats/INDEX.md`](formats/INDEX.md): Router to the format specs, concept notes and `.ksy` schemas: catalog of each format's magic, role, tier, spec and schema, the runtime asset graph, and community provenance.
- [`formats/all.md`](formats/all.md): `.ALL` bundle from `MAKEONE.EXE` ([FMT-ALL-CHUNKS]): u16 count, id table, u32 offsets with EOF sentinel, id ranges, palettes 0x8042 and 0x801E; shipped-game chunks are unchanged `.RES`/`.SMP` items.
- [`formats/flm.md`](formats/flm.md): `.FLM` film stream ([FMT-FLM-OPCODES]): FILM magic, 3-byte slice header (back-pointer, 50 Hz `tick_duration`), end-of-film epilogue, and opcodes create, interp, var_set, view_obj, credits, sound.
- [`formats/res.md`](formats/res.md): `.RES` archive ([FMT-RES-HEADER]): RS magic, `res_index` and `item_count` bytes, u32 offset table; prop archives carry a name table, scenery archives do not; compound keys and the index catalog.
- [`formats/sod-opcode-coverage.md`](formats/sod-opcode-coverage.md): Census work queue for Partial SOD shapes: `OP_ANIMATE` is drawn as sprites since #222 (the census no longer stops on it); two-vertex polygons, which stopped 7 more, are now drawn as lines; the films placing them, why seven side-view items export no whole model, and regeneration.
- [`formats/sod-opcodes.md`](formats/sod-opcodes.md): The 107-opcode `.SOD` table ([FMT-SOD-OPCODES]) dispatched as multiples of 9, numbered as Patch #3 numbers them (the unpatched build adds `0x033C`), the `OP_TAP`, `OP_ANIMATE` and `IFVIS`/`BVIS` facing-flag semantics, and si-tools readings kept as hypotheses.
- [`formats/sod.md`](formats/sod.md): `.SOD` model bytecode ([FMT-SOD-HEADER]): 0x000C magic, 10-byte header, power-of-two scale table (indices 18 and 19 seen in corpus), the collision list the header word at byte 8 points to (cubes, boxes and planes the ground and collision probe walks; 1,279 of the 2,516 stock shapes have one), VM overview, coplanar decal rule, `OP_IFVIS` as a facing gate.

## formats/auxiliary

- [`formats/auxiliary/anchorpt.md`](formats/auxiliary/anchorpt.md): `ANCHORPT.DAT` ([FMT-MAP-ANCHORPT]): 1,024 28-byte anchor records saved by `SD.EXE`, elevation stored negated; the game images hold the 231 authored records, and the eleven words are inferred cache.
- [`formats/auxiliary/map.md`](formats/auxiliary/map.md): `MAP.BIN` ([FMT-MAP-AREA]) patch pool and `REGIONS.BIN` block tree from `SD.EXE`: fields as list links and split distance, how `SD.EXE` compiles them into the scenery tree, eight unlinked patches.
- [`formats/auxiliary/pfont.md`](formats/auxiliary/pfont.md): `PFONT.BIN`: 1,152-byte font of a 128-byte width table and 128 8x8 one-bit glyphs, and the `PLAYONE.EXE` credits rule (centring, ink 255, shadow) that reproduces the `INTRO.FLM` title cards.
- [`formats/auxiliary/scenery.md`](formats/auxiliary/scenery.md): `SCENERY.scn` ([FMT-MAP-SCENERY]) is `PLAYONE.EXE`'s stack-segment scenery tree widened to 32-bit words; node types, the `SP_1NODE` level-of-detail rule, and prop height: ancestors' `SP_POS` `y` plus the shape's `ground_y_offset` scaled by its scale index.
- [`formats/auxiliary/set.md`](formats/auxiliary/set.md): `.SET` stage ([FMT-SET-HEADER]): 84-byte header, 67-byte events from 0x54, one 64-byte record per occupied prop slot (0-39); `TYPESET.EXE` operators and printed prop fields; 129 sets close.
- [`formats/auxiliary/sio.md`](formats/auxiliary/sio.md): `.SIO` SLICE modeller format ([FMT-SIO-RECORDS]): `Sds` magic, grid byte, 0x12 vertex and 0x06 midpoint records, `FF FF 00 00` trailer; the tool compiling `.SIO` to `.SOD` is unidentified.
- [`formats/auxiliary/spr.md`](formats/auxiliary/spr.md): `.SPR` image ([FMT-SPR-HEADER]): u16 width, height and encoding, then from byte 6 raw rows (encoding 0) or span-coded rows, no trailer; colour 0 is keyed transparent by the scaled `OP_ANIMATE` blit, copied by the unscaled draw; `PCX2SPR` writes pixels from byte 4, which the code would draw two pixels shifted (`[Hypothesis]`); the `MAKESPR` `.SOD` billboard wrapper.

## formats/concepts

- [`formats/concepts/compression.md`](formats/concepts/compression.md): DOS storage tiers: LZEXE 0.91 packing of `PLAYONE.EXE` and its LZSS bitstream, uncompressed retail `.RES` and `.ALL` payloads, PCX RLE in sprite sources, and the [I8] uppercase 8.3 path rules.
- [`formats/concepts/coordinates-and-units.md`](formats/concepts/coordinates-and-units.md): [I1] coordinate frames from model to screen: right-handed metric basis, 16.16 fixed point, BAM angles, `sod_scale_table`, editor units to metres, focal length and FOV, attribute-keyed vertex welding.
- [`formats/concepts/palette-and-shading.md`](formats/concepts/palette-and-shading.md): [I3] palette model: DAC scalings, palettes 0x8042 and 0x801E, colour groups and 32-level ramps, an unlit ground, `SHADES` lit by film variable 13's light, the sky drawer's bands 224-238, 256x32 LUT.
- [`formats/concepts/timeline-and-ticks.md`](formats/concepts/timeline-and-ticks.md): [I4] playback timing: 50 Hz PIT divisor 0x5D38, slice ticks as cumulative `tick_duration`, lerp and slerp sub-tick interpolation, shorter-arc roll, cut suppression, and 0x9C audio cues.

## formats/memory

- [`formats/memory/kaitai-memory-spike.md`](formats/memory/kaitai-memory-spike.md): Whether runtime memory records fit `.ksy`: `actor_record.ksy`, for the hypothesised [MEM-ACTOR-TABLE] layout, compiles and parses; `.ksy` is advised as layout source and check, not runtime parser.

## makeone-exe

- [`makeone-exe/driving.md`](makeone-exe/driving.md): How the harness drives `MAKEONE.EXE` under emulation to make a film's `.ALL`: keys, text-mode return as completion signal, a working mount, output checks, run time per CPU profile and hang policy.
- [`makeone-exe/linking.md`](makeone-exe/linking.md): A film's `.ALL` copies stock items verbatim, id-ordered by `(res_index << 8) | (segment + 1)`, music and common sounds by sound setting; stock shapes draw CTRY, INTRO and BALLOON like their archives in our renderer; on `PLAYONE` a superset with the palette items keeps the palettes, but some pages differ, as they do when the own archive is padded with inert chunks: not by content, nor by count, bytes or ids alone, but, on CTRY, once the padding makes the film's pages fall a whole film tick later (the smallest arms tried that change them: 368 one-byte chunks, 137,500 bytes in 63 chunks), and, in 34 captures, exactly when the pages fall on other emulator frames.

## parity

- [`parity/attribution.md`](parity/attribution.md): Splits the SSIM loss of the seven VAULT reference films by render layer: props lead on four and terrain on two, BALLOON's low mask IoU came from a straight-down camera we drew blank and a zenith sky outside the scorer's band, both since fixed, and a pre-decal CTRY window study puts most loss at edges, not flat colour.
- [`parity/batch-vault-films.md`](parity/batch-vault-films.md): Reads the ten retail vault films through the batch survey: the vision-model error readout, their render-store scores and capture rates, the suspects rescored on the stride plan, and the error readout of the seven Patch #3 references, whose 2026-11-22 baseline on lavapipe at `b9441a06` has no category at 3 of 12 frames and `sea-band-wrong` at 0 on all seven, against 7, 6 and 4 frames on three films on 2026-11-16.
- [`parity/batch.md`](parity/batch.md): Survey of corpus films through `mise run batch-parity`'s archive, capture, render and score stages: the score spread of the 79 of 529 scored when it stopped, stage costs, capture failures, rescores.
- [`parity/col3-2-studio.md`](parity/col3-2-studio.md): Records the COL3-2.FLM studio interior (anchorman, desk, window) that PLAYONE draws from tick 458 and we do not: evaluator state, actor clusters, shape census, and why the gap is unresolved.
- [`parity/evidence-limits.md`](parity/evidence-limits.md): Lists what the parity scores do not yet establish: film coverage, metric caveats, the non-deterministic reference, GPU and lavapipe differences, where a render's memory goes (its figures are in `lavapipe-render-time.md`), and what dosbox-automation captures can and cannot show.
- [`parity/film-segments.md`](parity/film-segments.md): Covers INTRO.FLM segments where PLAYONE shows a scene we do not: sand shots as SCENERY tiles, the montage clock and parked aircraft, and black title cards. The COL3-2 studio is in col3-2-studio.md.
- [`parity/framing-and-actors.md`](parity/framing-and-actors.md): Records the camera and projection corrections tried against the capture: square 256 px projection (adopted) and the eye-height, pitch, FOV, framing-offset and tick-phase sweeps that were ruled out; the `location` rotor drawn with its solid blades on every tick (#504, #624); and background misregistration, which is neither one time offset nor one page shift on the readout ticks, with a one-row vertical shift recurring (#990, #1027).
- [`parity/hero-aircraft-orientation.md`](parity/hero-aircraft-orientation.md): Records the actor orientation fixes for the CTRY.FLM hero aircraft: DOS rotation order, shapes that decode upside down, and the 48 axis-permutation sweep that ruled out other composition orders.
- [`parity/hero-aircraft-placement.md`](parity/hero-aircraft-placement.md): Records where the CTRY.FLM hero aircraft (shape 0x7F37) sits and how its body draws: position re-measures, SORTON subtrees, SHADE colour, ground offset, mesh vertices; the residual is open.
- [`parity/hero-shadow.md`](parity/hero-shadow.md): Records the actor ground shadow: the black silhouette the capture draws, where PLAYONE draws it from (slot flag, 0x19FC plane solve), the flattened-copy rule adopted in #206, the plane and height probe 0x240A, and the handbook's altitude cutoff, which in the frames sampled is the view cull of the shadow's ground point: in one film a high actor's shadow with its ground point in view reached the draw and the captured frame, and the view slot's own shadow, drawn when the cull kept it in the three slots read.
- [`parity/lavapipe-line-clip.md`](parity/lavapipe-line-clip.md): Lavapipe clips a line against the near plane but not the sides of the view, so an outline edge cut by the near plane beside the eye reaches its rasteriser tens of thousands of pixels off the page, five times farther at a 0.1 m near plane than at 0.5 m, and is drawn as a wedge (LAND 1025, 7,379 pixels). The outline line lists are clipped to a band 1.1 times the view through user clip distances, which lavapipe applies to lines: LAND's mean disagreement with the GPU falls from 309.42 to 5.23 pixels a tick, LOCATION's from 79.24 to 8.60, both below where they were before the near plane moved.
- [`parity/lavapipe-render-time.md`](parity/lavapipe-render-time.md): Which renderer changes cut headless render time on lavapipe and the GPU, where the time goes now, and what a render's memory goes to per worker. Landed: #596, #602, #644, #811, the view-facing cull #914 (52.4% to 80.6% of the Windows lavapipe loop in its probe), #933, #942, #943 and #944, and stuntreel --workers (#916): four child processes render LOCATION 1.85x faster on 4 vCPUs, while four in-process VkDevices sharing one instance regress on Ubuntu Mesa 25.2.8. On lavapipe the world's base and decal draws hold 49.0% of the whole LOCATION loop, on Span B mostly the decal fill-to-outline switch (by elimination); #1002's stack profile puts the whole LOCATION loop on lavapipe's queue thread (rasterizers 26.7%, vertex work 21.4%, line setup 14.6%, fragment-state store try_update_scene_state 10.2% and 28.3% of Span B, other state 8.5%, triangle setup 5.4%, submit 2.1%). #999's CPU probe sizes a frame-streamed world at up to 75,576 vertices, 76,008 indices and 149,956 outline indices a frame (INTRO tick 3635, 2.88 MiB vs LOCATION's 333.75 MiB baked). A LOCATION render's memory is mostly its world mesh (1,004 MiB Linux lavapipe peak vs CTRY's 139 MiB; release_world_mesh brings it to 749 MiB; each extra lavapipe device adds 751..796 MiB RSS). No-go: culling actors, #919, #915b, #926, #622, #920 and #1000.
- [`parity/lavapipe.md`](parity/lavapipe.md): Mesa's clipper can make the shade varying NaN; with the guard, local lavapipe scores within 0.002 of the GPU on all seven films. Eye-relative transforms, which take the eye's translation off each draw's matrix on the CPU, cut the per-tick difference by 46% to 84% on each film and shrink the four near-coplanar depth-tie residues to 17 pixels or fewer each; other ties remain. Reversed, infinite depth in `Depth24Plus` lowers it again on every film (LOCATION 62.0 to 29.8 pixels per tick); in `Depth32Float` it rose on five, and on all seven when re-measured after #904 and #922. Since #636 and #637 each same-layer index pair the GPU and the canonical lavapipe swap has at most 4 interior pixels on any tick of the seven films, so the decal bias stays for backend agreement (#638). Drawing LOCATION's castle green strip as a decal of its moat (#966) removed the strip-against-moat tie at LOCATION 3815 to 3830; the worst tick over 3812 to 3968 fell from 584 to 39 differing pixels. The screen-linear ratio `shade·w / w` makes the Gouraud polygons the clipper breaks draw the GPU's gradient (BALLOON 145 on `3a7afb76`: all 4,044 broken pixels match the GPU, 1,097 differing pixels in the frame become 7). Ubuntu 24.04's `mesa-vulkan-drivers` `25.2.8-0ubuntu0.24.04.5` drew the same index planes on an AMD Ryzen under WSL 2 as on a cloud container's Intel Xeon, on all 20,621 ticks of one tree; mesa-dist-win 25.2.8 differs from it by at most 33 pixels a tick. On `crates` `d897adcc` mesa-dist-win 26.2.6 differs from the canonical lavapipe on 118 to 1,407 ticks a film, by at most 359 pixels on a tick, and scores within 0.0000125 of it on every film at the seven decimals printed; most of the pixels 25.2.8 and 26.2.6 draw differently are single edge pixels. Render time is in its own note.
- [`parity/method.md`](parity/method.md): Defines the parity loop that judges a render change against PLAYONE.EXE: capture, render, SSIM and IoU scoring with the fade floor, compare verdicts, dead ends and how to read the legacy parity log.
- [`parity/metric-bench.md`](parity/metric-bench.md): Records how the parity metrics behave: the planted-fault metric bench, recapture noise of the reference films (with and without sound), and error categories graded by a vision model.
- [`parity/painter-order.md`](parity/painter-order.md): Drawing CTRY's base geometry in draw order with no depth test, as PLAYONE's painter does, scores below the depth buffer: SSIM 0.9184 to 0.9082 with nodes sorted back to front and 0.9068 in walk order, with worse index agreement on 103 and 91 of 114 frames; on this evidence, revisiting SPEC 2.1 is not worth an ADR.
- [`parity/probes.md`](parity/probes.md): Procedures for diagnosing one parity discrepancy: `parity_probe.py` crop, shift, iou, retime, index and register, `DBG_` switch sweeps via `mise run sweep`, capture-side experiments, and environment pitfalls.
- [`parity/prop-shape-loss.md`](parity/prop-shape-loss.md): Ranks the prop shapes costing LOCATION's and BOMB's props loss and why each loses: a late canyon camera step, per-shot camera offsets, in-shape cover order, far-town stand-ins, tick phase, lines; most of BOMB's street loss is unexplained.
- [`parity/render-model.md`](parity/render-model.md): Compares PLAYONE's back-to-front software painter with our depth-buffer renderer stage by stage, naming each known divergence and the `[I5]` ordered decal pass and ground-decal rules that imitate its tie order.
- [`parity/report-fields.md`](parity/report-fields.md): The keys and JSON types of the parity reports `report.json` and `compare.json`, checked against `stuntreel parity` output on synthetic fixtures by the `report_doc.rs` test.

## playone-exe

- [`playone-exe/angle-bank.md`](playone-exe/angle-bank.md): Bank words `0x10`..`0x14`, `0x18` and `0x1A` (`work:0x811E`..`0x8128`) are written once per frame for the whole film from the clock and film variables 10 and 12; only `0x16` is per actor. `BVGT` reads the bank too, and a rotor picks solid or line blades by word `0x12`; across the 31 retail/demo/FreeFlight archives no stock `ROT*` reads `0x10`, `0x12` or `0x16`, and no scenery or view-facing shape runs `ROT*`.
- [`playone-exe/capture-dosbox-automation.md`](playone-exe/capture-dosbox-automation.md): dosbox-automation 0.85.1 as capture emulator: frame-locked capture reading `film_tick` per frame at `DS = 0x0F46`, bit-identical `CTRY.FLM` runs with the demo archive, replays made to differ by sound samples in the archive, torn pages, DAC lag and the Lua instruction budget.
- [`playone-exe/capture-speed.md`](playone-exe/capture-speed.md): Historical DOSBox-X tests on `vault-balloon`: no tried setting, `turbo` or sampling cuts the 0.25 s frame cost, `nosound` freezes the clock, sampled tags lag 7 to 10 ticks; and where a capture ends.
- [`playone-exe/capture.md`](playone-exe/capture.md): Historical DOSBox-X debugger capture harness: link framing, crash constraints, BDA key injection, the `film_tick` tagging protocol, the one-tick page lag and an inferred 185-row 3D viewport.
- [`playone-exe/debugger-plans.md`](playone-exe/debugger-plans.md): How `mise run debug-x` breakpoint plans run on DOSBox-X: boot and key entry, image offset to live `CS:IP` mapping on both builds, the `BPM` watch filter that names a writer, and the hit loop.
- [`playone-exe/dosbox-x-legacy.md`](playone-exe/dosbox-x-legacy.md): What the retired DOSBox-X harness established, for reading old captures: link framing, debugger verbs and quirks, crash constraints, `DS = 0x1575`, late wall-paced tags and `dacexpand` rounding.
- [`playone-exe/film-load.md`](playone-exe/film-load.md): `PLAYONE.EXE` loading a film: the `.ALL` directory read, every chunk preloaded into an LRU cache whose node pool shrinks as the id index grows, what each chunk costs, the film clock starting on the first timer tick after the load, so archives that draw alike start on the same interrupt and later ones whole ticks later, and the per-frame probe that sweeps from each slot's position at the previous drawn frame, whose results in `CTRY.FLM` did not change at any probed frame of two live runs, while its padded-archive pages differ at the propeller and the viewpoint; the slots are placed by the fraction the film step sets from its clock reading and the HUD shows the clock after the render, and on 12 of the 23 viewpoint pages, on peaked score curves, the two archives' scenes are a tick apart at one tag.
- [`playone-exe/lod.md`](playone-exe/lod.md): The `SP_1NODE` distance gate at `0x2121` compares half the view-space depth, shifted right by the lens exponent `0x229E`, with a threshold scaled by `DS:0x22A4` (the `GAME.VAR` detail word times the lens mantissa); Patch #3 runs the same gate code; the renderer tests it per frame, and captures likely run at full detail.
- [`playone-exe/memory-map-main.md`](playone-exe/memory-map-main.md): `PLAYONE.EXE` `DS` data offsets, code addresses and the resident mixer setter: film variables and state, palette build and DAC upload, view setup, world light, matrix and draw routines.
- [`playone-exe/memory-map-patch3.md`](playone-exe/memory-map-patch3.md): Patch #3 `PLAYONE.EXE` counterparts of memory-map rows, unmapped ones marked: moved `DGROUP` offsets, unchanged work-segment offsets, and code addresses, paired function by function.
- [`playone-exe/memory-map-runtime.md`](playone-exe/memory-map-runtime.md): `PLAYONE.EXE` runtime capture anchors: the per-frame retrace trap, the 50 Hz tick and film clock, and the unverified camera-rig and actor-table layouts.
- [`playone-exe/memory-map-vm.md`](playone-exe/memory-map-vm.md): Offsets in the work segment of `PLAYONE.EXE`'s SOD display-list VM: anchor table, sine table, vertex arena, view matrices, lens and bank words, shadow mode, and VM code anchors.
- [`playone-exe/memory-map.md`](playone-exe/memory-map.md): Index of the `PLAYONE.EXE` memory-map files and the conventions they share, with the `DGROUP` offset table of the unpatched build: strings, flags, clocks, view and slot state.
- [`playone-exe/memory.md`](playone-exe/memory.md): Evidence for the memory map: `DS` per emulator, the [MEM-FLM-TICK] counters (film clock read equal to `0x22B8` until it holds), the unverified `0C5E` trap, [MEM-UNPACK-LOCKOUT] and image relocation.
- [`playone-exe/navigation.md`](playone-exe/navigation.md): How the `PLAYONE.EXE` LOAD FILM dialog works: a `VAULT` directory listbox with single-letter prefix jumps, `.FLM`/`.ALL` pairing, and harness key injection through the BIOS keyboard ring buffer.
- [`playone-exe/palette-fade.md`](playone-exe/palette-fade.md): Film variables 13-15, keyed by `var_set` and interpolated per frame, drive the palette build at `0x0FD2` (night, brightness, saturation), so the end-of-film fade is authored in the film.
- [`playone-exe/patch3.md`](playone-exe/patch3.md): What Patch #3 changes, the patched `PLAYONE.EXE` offsets mapped by function pairing (one dispatch slot fewer, inferred statically; the `SOD.H` opcode names number the patched build, and no census walk reaches the shifted opcodes), and which build each tested film needs to play and capture.
- [`playone-exe/scene-walk-actors.md`](playone-exe/scene-walk-actors.md): How the scenery walk places actors among world objects: the actor queue pushes one list at `DGROUP:0x4F00`, the plane nodes split it by the slot's position, and each entry is drawn just before or after the object of the `SP_LEAF` it reaches, or inside that object's display list at `OP_IPG` type 4 when its probe recorded a bucket there (`w` = twice a collision-box code); replayed for `CTRY` tick 871, from the image's tree or from the world's placement records, it draws the explosion after the tower and before the foreground hill, as the capture does; at `INTRO` tick 1398 the explosion and the vehicle beside it reach one leaf, so the depth sort orders them, by the depth of the slots' own positions; 83 of the 2,516 stock shapes carry a box coded 1 to 7, and 75 of them a matching bucket on their traced path.
- [`playone-exe/sod-animate.md`](playone-exe/sod-animate.md): `OP_ANIMATE` (`0x01F8`) blits frame `(count × bank word) >> 16` of its image table as a square centred on a projected point; selector `0x16` is the slot's interpolated `.FLM` animate word, `0x10` the film clock.
- [`playone-exe/sod-vm-execution.md`](playone-exe/sod-vm-execution.md): The SOD VM execution model: the vertex and vector banks, the transform stack, control flow, `SHADE` colour, the facing and depth gates, and the model frame of cube corners and `OP_VECTORS`.
- [`playone-exe/sod-vm-frame.md`](playone-exe/sod-vm-frame.md): The per-frame routine and scene composition: the 3D scene and credits, and the actor shadow draw (the plane probe `0x240A`, the flattened second draw in index 0, the `work:0x806C` readers, and the view cull `0x1B0C`, which drops a high actor's shadow when its ground point is out of view and, in the one film checked, passed it to the draw, and into the captured frame, when it was in view; the probe's ground plane does not depend on height; the view slot's own shadow, drawn when the cull kept it in the three slots read).
- [`playone-exe/sod-vm-generators.md`](playone-exe/sod-vm-generators.md): The SOD VM raw-coordinate generators: `PERFDISK`, the model frames and two-vertex polygons; lines and polygon spans are in their own note.
- [`playone-exe/sod-vm-lines-spans.md`](playone-exe/sod-vm-lines-spans.md): The SOD VM's lines and polygon spans: `MOVETO`/`ZLINETO`/`LINECOL` lines, polygon spans that include both ends, and the span test that culls an anticlockwise polygon with its outline, and the polygon clipper, which cuts at the view pyramid's sides and has no near plane.
- [`playone-exe/sod-vm.md`](playone-exe/sod-vm.md): The SOD display-list VM: self-patching dispatch slots, `OP_TAP` encoding and anchor loading [FMT-SOD-TAP], anchor records, register side effects, hill fins, HUGETAP and the Rust mapping.
- [`playone-exe/startup.md`](playone-exe/startup.md): `PLAYONE.EXE` startup: LZEXE 0.91 packing, a command tail that honours only `?` (runs `install.exe`), the `game.cfg`, memory and disk checks, asset paths, and how to reproduce the static analysis.
- [`playone-exe/static-tooling.md`](playone-exe/static-tooling.md): Which static tool answers which `PLAYONE.EXE` question (`mise run re-tool -- disasm`/`xref`/`callers`/`vm-handler`, Ghidra, rea), what Ghidra cannot see in the VM handlers, and the address coordinate conversions.
- [`playone-exe/terrain-shade.md`](playone-exe/terrain-shade.md): `GVPOLY`/`GVPOLY16` shade as a Gouraud ramp on the palette index (`idx = base + (s >> 9)`, `s >> 10` for `GVPOLY16`), lit by the world light the var-13 handler writes, turned as `R · L` for a rotated actor; the ground takes no light.
- [`playone-exe/world-scene-residuals.md`](playone-exe/world-scene-residuals.md): `PLAYONE`'s ground renderer residuals: scenery tiles lie on the terrain plane and tie it in depth, flat props are snapped onto it and painted in walk order, as is any prop face within 10 cm of the ground plane, a flat prop lying on an earlier flat prop is drawn after it as its decal, and a line on a decal now draws after it; the sub-pixel prop cull drops no drawn prop on the references, and the renderer drops far scenery per frame by distance against its `scale_index`, following `PLAYONE`'s cull `0x1B28` (`[Supported Inference]` for the distance in metres).
- [`playone-exe/world-scene.md`](playone-exe/world-scene.md): `PLAYONE` draws the ground flat from `MAP.BIN`-coloured leaves of a BSP scenery tree in its own image and, in live CTRY runs, paints `SCENERY2.RES` tiles over it, licensing our ground-decal pass; with no depth buffer it paints the flat ground in walk order, which our `WORLD_GROUND` pass follows in part.

## research

- [`handbook.md`](handbook.md): Source card for the retail handbook and its OCR text: how to cite it, why it is reliable for structure but not for numbers or units, its [Hypothesis] ceiling, and where each finding went.

## sd-exe

- [`sd-exe/image.md`](sd-exe/image.md): Reading the `SD.EXE` scenery designer image: MZ header and load-image offset rule, segments and DGROUP, string offsets, and routines for `ANCHORPT.DAT`, `MAP.BIN` and the `REGIONS.BIN` block tree.

## stunt-exe

- [`stunt-exe/sets.md`](stunt-exe/sets.md): `STUNT.EXE` evidence on `.SET`: neither `MAKEONE` nor `PLAYONE` names it, its display templates give the IF/AND/THEN vocabulary with operand widths; also the crack stub and TYPESET as dump oracle.
- [`stunt-exe/shadow.md`](stunt-exe/shadow.md): `STUNT.EXE`'s film shadow draw is `PLAYONE`'s code at a fixed offset, and its writers of the slot shadow flag (the prop editor's SHD toggle, the prop-to-slot build, a fixed setup, the film-stream create) compare no height.
